_comment: Ground truth for evaluating requirement 5. Each entry records a conflict deliberately planted across the corpus, the relationship type the detector should assign, which side the precedence policy should favour, and whether the answer must disclose the conflict to the user. eval/metrics.py scores detection precision/recall and resolution accuracy against this file.

conflicts.expected_resolution: Both are correct for their era: 3 in v2.4, 5 from v3.0 onward. Answer must state the current default and name the version change.
The highly-upvoted forum answer is wrong. Answer must correct it explicitly, because the user may already believe it.

claim_a.claim: zephyr dlq list (no payload flag documented)

conflicts.expected_resolution: Not a contradiction: the docs are silent, a staff forum post fills the gap. Forum wins on staff authority; answer should note it is undocumented.

claim_b.claim: the CLI is broken on Windows

conflicts.expected_resolution: Both true under different versions: broken in 3.0, fixed in 3.1. Answer must scope by version rather than pick a side.
Same-source conflict. Recency rule inside the docs tier: the changelog is authoritative, the reference page is stale.
Not a factual conflict: push() still works but is deprecated. Recommend enqueue(), note the old form is what they will see in older threads.

claim_b.claim: Retry-After is ignored and jobs retry forever

conflicts.expected_resolution: Three independent reports of observed behaviour outweigh silent deference to docs. Documented intent is 3.1+; the reports are 3.0. Answer must surface the discrepancy as a known issue, not hide it.
Header changed in v3.0. Current answer is X-Zephyr-Key; mention the old form for users upgrading.
Guest-authored blog is simply wrong, and was wrong when published. Docs win on authority; low author authority is the tie-breaker signal.
60s in v2.4, 30s from v3.0. Scope by version.
FALSE POSITIVE TEST. These describe different components: managed workers default to 10, self-hosted agents to CPU count. A good detector labels this complementary, not contradictory.

claim_b.claim: the DLQ replays automatically after an hour

conflicts.expected_resolution: Low-vote forum guess is wrong. Correct it; no automatic replay exists.

non_conflicts_for_false_positive_testing.note: Both describe exponential backoff with jitter in different words. Must NOT be flagged.
Blog adds operational practice on top of documented behaviour. Must NOT be flagged.
Same header, different level of detail.
